title: Logarithmic dynamic convex-hull line intersection queries
formal: Can a dynamic planar point set support insertions and deletions in O(log(n+2)) amortized time and exact convex-hull line-section queries in O(log(n+2)) worst-case time, using O(n+1) space?
definitions: Maintain a finite set S of distinct real-coordinate points in R², initially empty, under insertion of an absent point and deletion of a present point. A query gives a line ℓ={x:a·x=b} with a≠0. Return conv(S)∩ℓ as empty, a single point, or a closed segment specified by its two endpoints. Thus tangencies, hull-edge overlap, collinear S and |S|≤2 are covered without a general-position assumption. The hull of the empty set is empty. Only this intersection is requested, not the full hull boundary. Use a deterministic real-RAM with exact +,−,×,division by nonzero quantities, comparisons and memory access, with no floor or arbitrary real-bit extraction. Space is O(n+1) scalar/pointer cells for current n. Query time is worst-case; update time is amortized over arbitrary interleaved operations, with n taken as the larger size before and after an update. Initialization is O(1).
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of all stated guarantees, or prove the precise target impossible. State any complexity hypothesis used in a conditional impossibility.
context:
Brodal and Jacob support several standard hull queries in logarithmic time, but detecting whether a line intersects is weaker than locating its intersection endpoints.

The maintained open-problem page explicitly distinguishes the remaining line-stabbing query.
why: The line-intersection interface asks for geometric information not covered by optimal extreme-point query bounds.

import_provenance.original_statement: Can arbitrary planar-point insertions and deletions and queries for the two intersections of a line with their convex hull all be supported in O(log n) time using linear space? Amortized update time is permitted, but line-intersection queries should take worst-case logarithmic time.

sentences: Points may be inserted and deleted anywhere in the plane.
A query asks exactly where a line cuts the current convex hull.
The answer is empty, a point or a segment.
Degenerate point sets and tangencies are included.
Updates may amortize their cost, but every query must finish in logarithmic time.
